processing: Orthodox Darjeeling manufacture: withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, with the degree of oxidation varying by flush. The garden also makes some green tea.
harvest_season: First, second and autumn flushes; as across Darjeeling, first flush falls in spring and second flush in early summer.
appearance_dry: As with other orthodox Darjeelings, wiry mixed leaf, greener and paler in first flush and darker with golden tips in second flush.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in first flush, deepening to amber in second flush, typical of Darjeeling.
appearance_wet: Open, partly green leaf in first flush and more evenly coppery leaf in later flushes, as is usual in the district.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about Turzum in particular beyond flush names; expect the usual Darjeeling arc, from brisk and floral in spring to rounder and fruitier in summer.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western style. Use cooler water and a shorter steep for first flush, near-boiling water for second flush and autumn lots.

vintage_note: Sold by flush and year, usually with the invoice or lot name on the label, as with other Darjeeling gardens. First flush is the freshest and best drunk within the year; second flush and autumn teas keep a little longer.
description:
Turzum is a Darjeeling garden in the Rungbong valley near Sonada, and it is joined at the hip with its neighbour Sungma. The two have been run as one unit since the 1930s, so you will see either name on a packet, with both coming through the same factory.

The land runs from about 1,100 to 1,700 metres, which is a wide spread for one garden. It makes first, second and autumn flushes in the orthodox way, mostly black with some green, and it holds organic certificates for the Indian, American and Japanese markets.

For taste, go by flush rather than by garden name. As with other Darjeelings, spring lots are light and floral and punish boiling water and long steeps, while summer lots are rounder and take heat well.

Sellers usually give the flush, the year and a fanciful lot name such as Enigma or Moonlight. Those names belong to the lot, not to a separate kind of tea, so compare by flush and year first.
history:
Turzum and Sungma both date to the 1860s, with 1863 given by the current owner's side for the founding. An earthquake in 1934 destroyed the Sungma factory, after which the gardens were merged and all manufacture moved to Turzum.

The Jhunjhunwala family took over in the late 1950s, the Jindals bought the garden around 1975 and ran it for about sixteen years, and it then passed to the Jayshree Group, which still manages it.
